article.headline: Disney Rises 4.6% After Earnings Beat And $3 Billion Savings Plan
article.deck: The stock closed through the 119.88 buy point of a 62-week cup and sits 2.1% above it, inside the buy range to 125.87.
body: Disney rose 5.42 to 122.36, up 4.6%, and closed through the 119.88 buy point of a 62-week cup. The base ran from an Aug. 22, 2025 high to a March 27 low, a 23.0% correction, and the buy range runs to 125.87. The close sits 2.1% above the buy point and inside the range. Volume was 2.01x the 50-day average. After hours the stock was at 122.25, down 0.1%, as of 6:07 p.m. Eastern.

The stock closed 0.8% below its 52-week high of 123.37. It finished 11.2% above its 50-day line at 110.07 and 5.6% above its 21-day line at 115.83; the session's low held 0.28 ATRs above the 21-day line, so the move is not stretched. The RS line hit a new high, and Disney ranks 82 of 99 on the desk's list. Shares are up 7.6% this year and 15.8% over 12 months.

The latest quarter in the desk's table, June 2026, shows EPS of 1.51, down 48.3% from a year earlier, on revenue of $25.25 billion, up 6.8%. EPS across the four quarters shown ran 0.73, 1.34, 1.27 and 1.51. The next report is due Feb. 1.

Wednesday's headlines said Disney's earnings beat estimates and that the company laid out a $3 billion savings plan. TIKR counted 10 analysts raising targets; Bank of America went to $135 and JPMorgan to $140. The Motley Fool reported that the Experiences segment hit record quarterly revenue of $10.1 billion as cruise days surged. An earlier GuruFocus headline had the stock down 1.48% despite a 16% revenue jump and a 33% dividend hike.
A close back under 119.88 would leave the breakout stalled.
article.watch: Whether Disney holds above the 119.88 buy point while it trades inside the range that tops out at 125.87.

article.deck: A close through the 95.28 buy point of a 12-week cup put it in the buy range to 100.04, but the after-hours print slipped back below the buy point.
body: TransMedics gained 2.52 to 96.43, up 2.7%, and closed 1.2% above the 95.28 buy point of a 12-week cup. The base formed from an Aug. 21 high to an Oct. 30 low, a 32.1% correction, and the buy range runs to 100.04. Volume was 1.1x the 50-day average. After hours the stock traded at 94.90, down 1.6% and under the buy point, as of 5 p.m. Eastern.

The cup formed after a bigger slide: the stock is still well below its Dec. 2, 2025 high of 156.00, which gave way to a May 13 low of 60.10, and it sits 38.2% under that 52-week high. It closed 19.6% above its 50-day line at 80.64 and 5.9% above its 200-day at 91.03. The session's low held 1.89 ATRs above the 21-day line at 84.00, a firm trend but not a stretched one. TransMedics ranks 83 of 99 on the desk's list, though its RS line is 40.4% below its high. The stock is up 29.0% in a month and down 20.7% this year.

Revenue in the September quarter rose 41.1% to $203.0 million, while EPS of 0.46 was down 30.3% from a year earlier. Revenue has climbed in each quarter of the table, from $160.8 million in December 2025 to $173.9 million, $189.9 million and $203.0 million. EPS ran 2.62, 0.20, 0.41 and 0.46.

Recent headlines tracked the chart: Zacks noted the stock had reclaimed its 200-day line and flashed a golden cross, and an Insider Monkey piece said some experts think the company has a near-monopoly on keeping donor organs alive.
A close back under 95.28 would leave the breakout stalled.

article.headline: AMD Jumps 5.3% A Day After Nvidia's Earnings Beat
article.deck: The rebound left AMD 19.5% below the 658.62 buy point of a 6-week deep cup and still under its 50-day line, so there is no entry.
body: AMD rose 26.73 to 530.14, up 5.3%, on volume 1.22x its 50-day average. It is forming a 6-week deep cup that ran from an Oct. 6 high of 658.52 to a Nov. 5 low of 402.10, a 38.9% correction. The buy point is 658.62 with a buy range to 691.55; the close sits 19.5% below it.

Even after the gain the stock closed 4.5% below its 50-day line at 555.22, a line it has broken, and the desk carries it on its sell-signals list. It closed 1.2% above its 21-day line at 524.07, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line. The 200-day line at 427.18 sits 24.1% below the close. AMD ranks 99 of 99 on the desk's list, though its RS line is 12.8% below its high. The stock is up 147.5% this year and 120.4% over 12 months.

The September quarter brought EPS of 1.46, up 94.7% from a year earlier, on revenue of $13.38 billion, up 44.7%. Revenue ran $10.27 billion, $10.25 billion, $11.54 billion and $13.38 billion across the four quarters in the table, and EPS ran 0.92, 0.84, 1.38 and 1.46. The next report is due Feb. 2.
Yahoo Finance reported Tuesday that AMD, Broadcom and CoreWeave stocks were mixed on Nvidia's third-quarter earnings beat. Wednesday's gain came the next session.
A close back above the 50-day line would be the first repair; the buy point is still a long way off.
article.watch: The 50-day line at 555.22, which AMD has to retake before the base can do any work.

article.deck: The October breakout from a 27-week cup has not held: the stock is 9.0% under the 176.51 buy point and below its 50-day line, so there is no entry.
body: ExxonMobil fell 6.63 to 160.58, down 4.0%, on volume 1.28x its 50-day average. The stock broke out Oct. 14 past the 176.51 buy point of a 27-week cup that ran from a March 30 high to a June 25 low, a 23.5% correction; the buy range ran to 185.34. Twenty-five sessions later the close sits 9.0% below the buy point, a stalled breakout. After hours the stock was at 160.63, flat.

The drop took the stock 5.3% under its 50-day line at 169.58 and 5.6% under its 21-day line at 170.06, with the session's high 0.76 ATRs below the 21-day line. It still holds 2.5% above its 200-day line at 156.72 and is 14.8% below its 52-week high of 188.50. ExxonMobil ranks 62 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 18.9% below its high. The stock is down 9.7% over the past month and up 33.4% this year.

The September quarter brought EPS of 3.72, up 111.4% from a year earlier, on revenue of $110.50 billion, up 32.6%. EPS in the table ran 1.53, 1.00, 3.48 and 3.72, with revenue going from $80.04 billion and $83.16 billion to $114.53 billion and $110.50 billion. The market cap is $655.04 billion and the forward P/E is 12.9. The next report is due Jan. 29.

A Motley Fool headline Wednesday said ExxonMobil had achieved something 95% of S&P 500 members haven't done; none of the day's headlines explains the drop. Energy is weak across the desk's list, with 7% of the group's names above their 50-day lines.
The chart needs a recovery of the 50-day line or a new base before there is a setup.

article.deck: A bounce off the 50-day line leaves the stock 9.8% under the 24.10 buy point of a deep 56-week cup, with an early entry at 21.42 already cleared.
body: SailPoint rose 1.57, or 7.8%, to 21.75 as of 11:17 a.m. Mountain after the session's low touched the 50-day line at 20.22. The stock is in a 56-week deep cup, 57.1% from a rim on Oct. 6, 2025, to a low of 10.30 on April 10, 2026, with a buy point of 24.10 and a buy range to 25.31. It sits 9.8% below the buy point. Volume is on pace for 0.4x its 50-day average.

Two early entries are live. The stock has cleared the 21.42 handle high from Nov. 11, the early entry ahead of the 24.10 buy point. The 50-day bounce gives another: a move above today's high of 21.95, 0.9% overhead, with the 50-day line as the stop.

SailPoint trades 3.8% below its 52-week high of 22.62, 7.6% above its 50-day line and 33.8% above its 200-day line at 16.26. It sits 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line at 20.43 because the day's low reached it, so the trend is intact and nothing is stretched. RS rank is 92 of 99 on the desk's list; the RS line is 5.8% below its high.

The company sells identity-security software. Revenue rose 16.8% to $308.8 million in the quarter ended July 31, and it lost 9 cents a share, after losses of 13 cents, 6 cents and 6 cents in the three quarters before. The next report is due Dec. 8. SailPoint is valued at $12.4 billion, at 53.96 times forward earnings.

article.headline: SailPoint Jumps 10.3% As Identity-Security Software Names Rally
article.deck: The stock bounced off its 50-day line to within 2.2% of its 52-week high and sits 7.7% below the 24.10 buy point of a 56-week deep cup.
body: SailPoint sells identity security to large organizations: software that sets, controls and automates the policies deciding who and what can reach a company's data and applications. It covers employees, contractors and machine identities alike, and it doubles as a regulatory-compliance tool.

The stock rose 2.07 to 22.25 on Wednesday, up 10.3%, on volume 1.09x its 50-day average, and added 1.5% to 22.59 after hours as of 6:11 p.m. Eastern. It moved with its corner of software: Okta rose 12.1%, Palo Alto Networks 9.9% and CrowdStrike 7.9% in the regular session.

The quarters show a growing business that is not yet profitable. Revenue in the July 2026 quarter rose 16.8% to $308.8 million, after $281.9 million, $294.6 million and $280.1 million in the three quarters before it. The company lost 9 cents a share, against losses of 6, 6 and 13 cents in those quarters. The next report is due Dec. 8.

The market values SailPoint at $12.70 billion. With no trailing earnings there is no trailing P/E; the forward P/E is 55.2. The stock is up 10.0% this year and 20.3% over 12 months. It ranks 94 of 99 on the desk's list, and its RS line is 3.6% below its high.

The base is a 56-week deep cup that began at an Oct. 6, 2025 high, fell 57.1% to a 10.30 low on April 10 and has climbed back to within 2.2% of the 52-week high of 22.74. The buy point is 24.10 with a buy range to 25.31. Wednesday's low touched the 50-day line at 20.23 and the stock closed 10.0% above it, 8.7% above the 21-day line at 20.47 and 36.8% above the 200-day at 16.26, a reading of 0.0 ATRs from the 21-day line.

The desk flags two earlier entries. The stock has already cleared the 21.42 handle high from Nov. 11 and closed 3.9% above it. The second is the 50-day bounce: a move above Wednesday's high of 22.84 is the early entry, with the 50-day line as the stop. Both come before the standard 24.10 buy point, and the Dec. 8 report falls inside that window.
In the news feed, Zacks ran a piece Tuesday weighing BILL against SAIL as a value stock. The other headlines in the feed are about other companies.
article.watch: Wednesday's 22.84 high first, then the 24.10 buy point, with the Dec. 8 report ahead.

chief.verdict: The leaders are thin and the market is still under pressure: the S&P 500 sits 4.2% under its 50-day line and the Nasdaq 6.9% under, with 7 and 6 distribution days in 25 sessions. Only four names broke out this week, and only Disney did it the right way, on 2.01 times normal volume with its RS line at a new high. The rest of today's stories are a weak-volume breakout extended from its 50-day (TMDX) and two former leaders, AMD and XOM, cracking the 50-day line. Risk leans down; this is a tape for one or two small positions, not a full book.
chief.market: Market in correction with 7 distribution days on the S&P 500 (weighted 6.8) and 6 on the Nasdaq (weighted 7.2): keep exposure light, mostly cash, and size any new buy as a pilot position until a follow-through day.

picks.why: A 62-week cup, 23.0% deep, cleared on 2.01 times its 50-day volume, closing at 122.36 within 0.8% of the 52-week high of 123.37, with the RS line at a new high. It is the only story with a perfect technical read (all five desk checks) and earnings are not due until 2027-02-01, so no report sits inside the trade. The risk is the fundamentals: latest-quarter EPS fell 48.3% from a year ago on 6.8% revenue growth, and a breakout in a correcting market fails more often.
picks.entry: In the buy range from 119.88 to 125.87; it closed 2.1% over the buy point at 122.36. Confirmation is a hold above 119.88 on the next sessions; a close back under 119.88 means the breakout failed, cut it.

picks.why: A 15-week flat base with RS rank 92 and the close at 1448.12, 2.0% over the 1420.01 buy point, is the tightest-looking pattern on the lists and the industrial group's top leader. Flat bases hold up better than deep cups in a correction. The risk is the group: industrials average an RS of 42 with only 24% of the group above the 50-day line.
picks.entry: Buy range 1420.01 to 1491.01; take it only on an up day with volume above average that keeps it over 1420.01, and skip it if it closes under 1420.01.

picks.why: RS rank 94, RS line 3.6% off its high, and today's 10.3% jump off the 50-day line make it the best-acting name on the aggressive list. But the base is a 57.1% deep cup, loose by any standard, and the company still loses money (EPS -0.09 last quarter), so this is not a stock to start early in a correction. Earnings on 2026-12-08 fall before the 24.10 buy point is likely to be tested.
picks.entry: The live aggressive entry is above today's high at 22.84 with the 50-day line at 20.23 as the stop; wait for the market to turn before using it. The proper buy point is 24.10, buy range to 25.31.

avoid.why: The breakout over 95.28 came on only 1.1 times normal volume, the stock is 19.6% above its 50-day line and 1.89 ATRs extended, the RS line is 40.4% below its high, and after hours it already traded back to 94.90, under the buy point.
RS rank 99, but it broke the 50-day line at 530.14 (4.5% under it) inside a 38.9% deep cup, 19.5% below the 658.62 buy point; that is a leader repairing, not a setup.
The October breakout over 176.51 has failed: it fell 4.0% today on 1.28 times volume through the 50-day line and closes 9.0% below the buy point.
It sits in the buy range 4.0% over its 254.99 buy point, but earnings are due 2026-11-19, tomorrow, and buying a flat base the day before a report is a coin flip, not an entry.

chief.watch: Whether Disney holds above its 119.88 buy point while the Nasdaq, up 0.4% today but 6.9% under its 50-day line, tries to put in a follow-through day.
